@graph.name: Port of Virginia Logistics Dataset
@graph.description: The per-port dataset for the Port of Virginia in the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the four Norfolk Harbor terminals — Norfolk International Terminals (NIT) and Virginia International Gateway (VIG), the port’s container terminals; Newport News Marine Terminal (NNMT), its primary RoRo and breakbulk terminal; and Portsmouth Marine Terminal (PMT), recorded as what it is, a deep-water heavy-lift and offshore-wind hub, not a container terminal. Richmond Marine Terminal (RMT), formerly recorded in this file as a covered facility, carries its own per-port dataset (datasets-richmond-marine-terminal.json) and hub page since the ports-completion build (2026-11-10) Virginia International Gateway is recorded as leased, not port-authority-owned. Each entity carries authority and operator of record, terminal facts with their sources, cargo specialties, rail service with on-dock and interchange qualifiers, highway corridors, foreign-trade-zone facts, labeled volume figures with period and source (the Port of Virginia system moved 3,499,639 TEUs in FY2024 and 3,239,638 TEUs in calendar 2025; no standalone volume is published for Richmond Marine Terminal because none is published by the port), current status items, and the branch binding that assigns the port to the Winchester, VA branch by verified road distance (Norfolk about 222 miles). The companion coverage node maps the port's 8 coverage cells. The company’s crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards. The offer set does not include drayage: freight moves on the customer’s or carrier’s trucks, and the company’s crews do the hands-on work at port-adjacent warehouses, receivers’ docks, yards, leased space, and on-terminal only by arrangement through the terminal’s own processes. Every fact carries its source.

@graph.name: Port of Virginia Service Coverage Dataset
@graph.description: The service-coverage cells for the Port of Virginia in the Ports & Intermodal program: 8 cells — the eight attached services (transloading; ocean container packing and unpacking; loading and unloading / container labor; cross-docking; freight rework; specialized workforce; logistics project management; 3PL support services) — each recording whether the service is offered, the treatment the program gives it (S, a dedicated spoke page; H, a hub section on /port-of-virginia-logistics/; D, dataset presence only), the delivery points, and the bound branch. Norfolk: transloading and ocean container work carry spoke treatment (the container-labor spoke is live), the remaining six services are hub sections. Delivery points come from one enum only: port-adjacent warehouse, receiver’s dock, yard, leased space, and on-terminal by arrangement — on-terminal work happens only by arrangement through the terminal’s own processes, never as a bare claim. The port binds to Winchester, VA.

@graph.name: Port of Virginia — Norfolk Harbor
@graph.description: Port of Virginia — Norfolk Harbor (Norfolk, VA) — deepwater marine port (container, RoRo, breakbulk). Authority: Virginia Port Authority. Operator: Virginia International Terminals, LLC (operating arm of the Virginia Port Authority). Cargo: containers (NIT, VIG); RoRo and breakbulk (NNMT — the port's primary RoRo and breakbulk terminal); offshore-wind and heavy-lift project cargo (PMT). Rail: Norfolk Southern — on-dock at NIT and VIG; CSX — on-dock at NNMT and PMT; intermodal access at NIT. Highway corridors: I-64, I-264, I-464, I-664. Foreign-trade zone: FTZ 20 (grantee Virginia Port Authority). U.S. Customs port of entry. Volume (FY2024, fiscal (Jul 2023-Jun 2024)): 3,499,639 TEU — Port of Virginia system (source: AJOT, Virginia FY2024 results, via ports program dossier §1.2). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 3,239,638 TEU — Port of Virginia system (source: Ports program dossier §1.2 (calendar 2025, -8.1%)). Volume (FY2024, fiscal): 283,817 short tons — Port of Virginia breakbulk tonnage (source: AJOT, Virginia FY2024 results, via ports program dossier §1.2). Branch binding: this port is served from the Winchester, VA branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 222 road miles from Winchester and 245 from Martinsburg; bound to Winchester on miles. about 23 mi / 25-40 min closer from Winchester.
